explanations.content: When a variable of a reference type is declared, it holds the address of the object in memory. Assigning one reference variable to another copies the reference, so both variables point to the same object. Updating the object through any reference is reflected when accessed via the other reference.

explanations.topic: Reference types in Java store a reference (address) to an object in memory rather than the actual object value.
